title: devserve: stable and per-worktree app servers as systemd user services
description:
## Idea (not yet specced)
House tooling so web apps run without tmux server windows: each app's main runs as an installed release under systemd user units on a fixed port (beads-board's two units on 4747 are the model), and each worktree branch can run as a transient preview server (systemd-run --user) on a port from the app's range, with its own dev database. Logs stay in journald and can be followed in a tmux pane on demand.

Sketch of the CLI: devserve up <app> [worktree] (pick a port, start, print the URL), devserve ls (all apps: branch, port, URL, state), devserve logs <name> (journalctl --user -f), devserve down <name> [--drop-db]. systemd is the registry: unit names and their environment hold app, branch and port; no extra state file.

## Why
The user wants to use their apps (beads-board, we-go-next, gw2) day to day on stable ports while trying features from worktrees on others, without tmux windows full of servers, and still be able to tail a server like an in-pane server.

## Questions for the spec
- Per-app entries: where they live (a TOML in the skills repo or each app's own file), port ranges, start command per app type (mix phx.server, release), database naming and cleanup.
- Previews: dev server from source vs a built release; env and secrets (no secrets in unit names or args; untracked env files only).
- Integration: dispatch briefs use devserve instead of "pick another port"; build sessions take screenshots from a real preview; beads-board shows a preview link per ticket or PR later.
- Lifecycle: previews stop when the worktree is removed; stale previews listed by devserve ls.
- Stable installs: a shared helper for release install and update (beads-board README steps generalised) or per-app only.
notes: 2026-10-18 (user): previews are never started automatically (not by dispatch, not by sessions). The board launches a preview from the ticket sheet on demand and stops it when the ticket moves forward (past review: merged, done or abandoned), so no orphan servers. devserve is the mechanism the board calls; the board owns when.

title: Explore training house skills with SkillOpt
description:
## Idea (not yet specced)
Try microsoft/SkillOpt (MIT, v0.2.0, PyPI; https://github.com/microsoft/skillopt) on the house skill set. SkillOpt treats a skill document as the trainable state of a frozen agent: an optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits, and keeps an edit only if a held-out validation score strictly improves. Output is a best_skill.md; no weight changes and no extra calls at inference. It runs Claude Code CLI and Codex CLI as rollout harnesses (exec backends), with a WebUI monitor and a preview nightly self-evolution mode.

## Why it might fit
Our skills are plain SKILL.md files with known failure modes we already correct by hand (lessons skill, retro findings, review rules). A scored loop could tune the ones with measurable outcomes instead of editing on anecdote.

## Questions to settle before specing (this is an initiative, not tickets yet)
- Which skills have a scoreable outcome? Candidates: code-review (findings caught on seeded diffs), to-tickets (coverage of a spec's checks), tight-spec (builder-check question count), dispatch (sessions that finish vs hand off early).
- What is a benchmark here: a skillopt env package per skill (adapter, data loader, scored rollout, YAML), built from our own past sessions, specs and diffs.
- Cost and harness: Claude Code CLI vs pi with GPT-6 Astra as the rollout agent; optimizer model choice; token budget per run.
- How optimized output re-enters the repo: as a reviewed diff to SKILL.md through the normal gates (check.py, catalog provenance, a house edit note), never auto-applied; how adapted/merged skills keep upstream sync working.
- Guardrails: rollouts in scratch worktrees only, no pushes, no real repos touched; the house hooks stay on.
- Is nightly self-evolution (SkillOpt-Sleep) wanted later, or only manual runs?

## Done when (for the initiative's first step)
A spike verdict on one skill: benchmark built, a baseline score, an optimized skill with its score, the diff reviewed, and a go/no-go for the rest.

title: Optional: weekly scheduled report-only skills-sync agent
notes:
Proposal (2026-10-16, gaps pass): who runs the maintenance loops (skills-sync, correct, retro, maintain-verification-skill). Nothing is scheduled yet.

(a) Weekly coordinator ritual, triggered by the user with one prompt in the coordinator session:

  Weekly upkeep, report-only: change nothing until I approve each item. 1) skills-sync: fetch and write this week's report; list candidates, file no beads, bump no pins. 2) Lessons: list `lesson` beads from the past week in every repo with .beads (dispatch's fd loop, `bd list -l lesson`); flag any mistake that repeated or sits at rung 3-4 and propose a higher rung. 3) correct: name the repo with the most corrections this week and the mistake classes you would fix there; do not fix. 4) maintain-verification-skill: for each repo with a verify skill, say whether code changed without its feature map (form-engine: `verify closeout --base <last week's sha>`) and whether a pass is due. 5) retro: only on a session I name. End with one table: loop, finding, proposed change, needs my decision (y/n).

(b) Automated weekly report-only run: a user crontab entry (WSL cron must be running; a laptop asleep or WSL shut down skips the week) that runs `python3 ~/dev/utils/skills/scripts/sync.py` (no --file-beads, no --bump) and writes reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md, optionally followed by a headless `claude -p` that reads the report and the week's lesson beads and writes a summary under drafts/. May: fetch sources, write reports/ and drafts/. May not: edit skills or catalog.toml, file or close beads, bump pins, commit, push, touch harness dirs. Claude Code cloud routines (/schedule) do not fit: they cannot see ~/dev, local skill-sources, or the local Dolt beads.

Recommendation: (a). Only skills-sync's fetch-and-diff is mechanical; correct, retro and maintain-verification-skill need judgment and the user's decisions, and their output is a decision list the user has to read anyway. (b) adds a cron dependency on WSL being up, and a headless run whose summary still waits for the user. Revisit (b) for sync.py alone if the ritual gets skipped for weeks.
